github.abstract: FreeLLMAPI 10.1 billion tokens per month.  87 free LLM providers. 1,313 free model endpoints. One OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Aggregate free tiers from dozens of providers, plus custom OpenAI-compatible chat, embedding, image, and audio endpoints, behind a single /v1 API. Keys are stored encrypted. A router picks the best available model for each request, falls over to the next provider when one is rate-limited, and tracks per-key usage so you stay under every free-tier cap. freellmapi.co · browse the full catalog: 736 model families, 1,313 free endpoints English · Türkçe · 簡體中文 · Русский · O'zbekcha Your router updates its own model catalog from a signed feed: new free models, quota changes, and compatibility fixes land without a git pull . Free installs get the monthly snapshot, so a model reaches them 30 days after it joins the live feed; premium routers get it the same day. Go live at freellmapi.co ($19/yr, cancel anytime). Contents Why this exists Supported providers Compatible CLIs & coding agents How it compares Features Quick start Desktop app Works with OpenAI-compatible clients Languages Premium (live catalog) Using the API Screenshots How it works FAQ Limitations Contributing Disclaimer Guides: Install & deploy · API reference · Clients & coding agents · Prompt compression · Architecture & internals · Documentation index · Contributor guide Why this exists Every serious AI lab now offers a free tier, a few million tokens a month, a few thousand requests a day. On its own each tier is a toy. Stacked together, they add up to roughly 10.1 billion tokens per month of working inference capacity, across 736 model families / 1,313 provider endpoints from small-and-fast to reasonably capable. The problem is that stacking them by hand is painful: eighty-seven different SDKs, eighty-seven different rate limits, eighty-seven places a request can fail. FreeLLMAPI collapses that into one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Point any OpenAI client library at your local server, and it routes transparently across whichever providers you've added keys for. And the free-tier landscape shifts weekly: providers launch models, retire them, and change quotas without notice. FreeLLMAPI tracks all of that for you. The router pulls a signed model catalog from freellmapi.co on its own, so your install keeps up without a git pull . See Premium (live catalog) for how fast it keeps up. Supported providers Google Groq Cerebras OpenCode Zen Mistral OpenRouter Cloudflare Cohere Z.ai (Zhipu) NVIDIA HuggingFace ModelScope Qwen3 · DeepSeek V4 · GLM-5 (needs Aliyun cn binding) … and 75 more free providers Plus a custom provider — point chat, embedding, image, or audio models at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, a local Ollama, or a remote gateway) from the Keys page. The full, always-current list lives at freellmapi.co/models with per-model rate limits, context windows, and free-token budgets. Compatible CLIs & coding agents Claude Code Codex CLI Gemini CLI Cursor Cline Roo Code OpenCode Aider … plus Continue, Goose, Qwen Code, Kilo Code, Crush, Zed, JetBrains AI, DeepSeek Harness, MiMo Code, AtomCode, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Pi, Reasonix, ZCode and any OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini or Ollama client Most agents configure themselves with one command that reads your live catalog, backs up the existing config and merges into it: npx freellmapi setup-claude --url http://localhost:3001 --api-key < unified-key > All supported agents and their setup commands → · Per-tool recipes, MCP server and URL tokens → How it compares Based on public documentation, July 2026 — corrections welcome. Features Every OpenAI-style surface — /v1/chat/completions , /v1/responses (what Codex CLI needs), /v1/completions (editor ghost-text autocomplete), /v1/images/generations , /v1/videos/generations , /v1/audio/speech , /v1/audio/transcriptions , /v1/embeddings , and /v1/models — streaming and non-streaming, from the official SDKs or any OpenAI-compatible client. API reference → Anthropic Messages API — /v1/messages speaks Anthropic's wire format over the same router, so Claude Code and the official Anthropic SDKs run against your free pool. Details → Native Gemini + Ollama surfaces — Gemini CLI can use /v1beta ( generateContent , streaming, token counting, models), while opt-in Ollama emulation serves NDJSON chat/generate, tags, metadata, and embeddings for Zed, JetBrains, and other local-model clients. Fusion (multi-model synthesis) — request the virtual fusion model and the router fans your prompt out to a panel of diverse free models in parallel, then a judge model synthesizes one answer from the drafts. Details → Image, video & speech generation — /v1/images/generations , /v1/videos/generations , and /v1/audio/speech route across the providers that serve media models; images and speech also accept custom OpenAI-compatible media endpoints. Video jobs are normalized across synchronous and queued providers and return a completed MP4. Tool calling & structured outputs — OpenAI-style tools round-trip across providers (plain-text tool calls are rescued into real tool_calls ), plus response_format , seed , logprobs , penalties, and the rest of the sampling params passed through per provider. Smart routing, six strategies — live per-model speed/capability/reliability scores rank your chain; automatic fallover retries the next model on 429/5xx with cooldowns and key rotation. Routing in detail → Unified models & profiles — the same model on several providers collapses into one entry with strict in-group failover; named fallback-chain profiles (a coding chain, a vision chain) switch from the dashboard or per request via auto:<profile> , and custom chains can be renamed in place from the chain manager. Per-key rate tracking — RPM/RPD/TPM/TPD counters per (platform, model, key) that learn providers' reported ceilings, so routing always stays under every cap. Self-updating model catalog — the router syncs a signed catalog from freellmapi.co twice a day: new models, quota changes, and provider quirk fixes land automatically. Free installs track the monthly snapshot, which each model joins 30 days after it lands in the live feed; premium routers get it same-day. Premium → Sticky sessions & context handoff — conversations stay on one model for 30 minutes; an optional compact handoff note keeps the thread coherent when a mid-chat switch does happen. Details → Prompt compression (opt-in) — a shared, fail-open request pipeline can deduplicate prompts, filter tool output, compact repeated JSON, and trim stale context before cache lookup and routing. Details → Encrypted keys, one token out — provider keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted in SQLite and decrypted in-memory per request; your apps only ever see a single unified freellmapi-… bearer token. Admin dashboard & analytics — React UI to manage keys, reorder the chain, run a playground, and read p50/p95/TTFT analytics over 24h–90d windows; login-gated, dark/light themes, 60 languages . ChatGPT-ready MCP server & interactive docs — ChatGPT and other MCP clients can call FreeLLMAPI inference, list usable models, inspect provider health/usage/cache/routing metadata, and manage the routing strategy over /mcp ; a dependency-free OpenAPI viewer lives at /v1/docs . ChatGPT and coding agents → Ops niceties — opt-in response cache, encrypted DB backups, periodic key health checks, bulk key import/export, declarative startup config. Install & deploy → Runs anywhere Node 20+ runs — Windows, macOS, Linux servers, or a small ARM SBC (Raspberry Pi included). ~40 MB RSS at idle behind PM2 / systemd / whatever supervisor you prefer. The scope is deliberately narrow — see what's not supported yet . Quick start One-liner (Docker required — sets up ~/freellmapi , generates an encryption key, pulls the image, and starts the container): curl -fsSL https://freellmapi.co/install.sh | bash Prefer to read before you pipe to bash? The script is here .

github.abstract:
深入理解 AI Infra：量化分析與系統設計 簡體中文 · English · 繁體中文 · Русский — community edition Tip 下載與閱讀 · 格式與版本說明 簡體中文（原版，作者 @bojieli ） ： PDF · EPUB · 線上閱讀 English（社群翻譯， @tg1482 ） : PDF · EPUB · Read online 繁體中文（社群翻譯， @edward821220 ） ： PDF · EPUB · 線上閱讀 Русский — community edition, @ilkruglov : PDF · EPUB · Онлайн-чтение · О переводе 《深入理解 AI Infra》是 GitHub 上獲得 50k+ Star 的 《深入理解 AI Agent：設計原理與工程實踐》 的姊妹篇。 寫完 《深入理解 AI Agent》 後，在與讀者交流的過程中，我越來越感到：要開發好基於模型的應用，還需要理解它賴以執行的基礎設施。大多數軟體工程師不必親自開發作業系統、編譯器和晶片，卻仍要學習作業系統、編譯原理和計算機體系結構，因為申請記憶體、讀取檔案、呼叫函式，背後都有資源與時間代價。基於模型開發應用也是如此。延遲相差幾倍，產品體驗就可能完全不同；成本相差一個數量級，能夠支撐的商業模式也隨之改變。 更深層的變化是 程式設計抽象的上移：從作業系統到模型上下文 。傳統的作業系統、編譯器和硬體要為事先未知的各種程式提供通用能力，系統最佳化總要在可程式設計性與效能之間取捨。如今 LLM 成了最重要的應用，從運算元執行到分散式排程，都可以針對特定的模型和加速器架構最佳化；模型設計也開始反過來適應硬體，DeepSeek V4/V4.1 重新設計長上下文的表示方式，就是一例。從某種意義上說， 模型成了 LLM 時代的作業系統，AI Infra 成了 LLM 時代的計算機體系結構 。《計算機體系結構：量化研究方法》是我在體系結構領域的入門書，而 AI Infra 領域還缺少一本從硬體約束和模型架構出發、量化推導系統設計的書，這是我寫作本書的動機。 貫穿全書的方法是 從約束推導設計 ：先明確任務與質量要求，列出計算、儲存、通訊和依賴關係，對照硬體的容量、頻寬和算力做數量級估算。這類估算人容易出錯，AI 也一樣：只算權重讀取而忘了 KV 快取，按峰值算力推算速度而不查頻寬能否供給，把工作平分給多張卡卻遺漏卡間通訊，漏掉任何一項，結論都可能偏離幾倍甚至幾個數量級。估算還有另一層用意：讀博時導師張霖濤博士反覆叮囑，最佳化一定要做到物理所允許的極限。本書貫徹這一習慣，先按第一性原理算出硬體允許的上限，再看實測離上限還有多遠；差距不是模型漏了項，就是系統有可以去掉的開銷。從 FPGA 加速 Bing 搜尋排序、昇騰 AKG 運算元生成到 UB 萬卡互聯，我反覆遇到的是同一條線索： 資料搬移 。本書因此反覆追問五個問題： 搬什麼、搬多少、搬幾次、經過哪裡、誰必須等它。 更多寫作背景見 前言 。 目前書稿仍是初稿，正在持續修訂。 內容目錄 章 主題 主要問題 1 初識 AI Infra 一次生成需要多少視訊記憶體、計算和資料讀寫？ 2 模型架構 注意力、歷史狀態與專家結構如何改變系統需求？ 3 推理與訓練負載 任務階段、到達模式和狀態壽命如何影響資源需求？ 4 加速器架構 如何在計算、儲存、頻寬、功耗與成本之間取捨？ 5 運算元與執行時 融合、複用、併發和排程如何減少執行開銷？ 6 超節點 多裝置協作如何平衡容量、吞吐和同步代價？ 7 資料中心網路 網路頻寬、通訊方式和擁塞如何影響計算效率？ 8 推理最佳化 批處理、KV 管理、卸載與推測解碼何時有效？ 9 分散式推理 如何放置計算和狀態，並處理擴縮容與恢復？ 10 訓練系統 如何安排視訊記憶體、通訊和重算，讓訓練更高效？ 11 資源排程與執行環境 模型服務和工具環境如何共享資源，減少等待？ 12 端邊雲協同 任務放在本地、邊緣還是雲端，如何兼顧效果、延遲和成本？ 適合誰讀 如果你已經呼叫過模型 API，或在自己的機器上執行過模型，想進一步弄清模型為什麼慢、如何降低成本，這本書可以作為起點。從事系統、網路和晶片工作的工程師，以及相關方向的研究人員和學生，也能從書中看到各層設計與實際模型任務的聯絡。 閱讀時需要一些 Python、線性代數和計算機系統基礎，具體要求見 前言 。建議先讀第 1—3 章，瞭解模型與負載，再根據自己的興趣選擇重點： 做模型應用和推理服務，可以重點讀第 8、9 章，再看第 11、12 章的任務環境與部署；遇到容量、運算元或通訊問題時，回到第 4—7 章追蹤原因。 做系統或網路，可以重點讀第 5—7 章，再看第 9、10 章，檢查這些機制如何影響分散式推理與訓練。 做晶片與體系結構，可以重點讀第 4—7 章，並結合後續章節的任務算例，檢查硬體指標如何轉化為實際的服務能力。 希望系統學習，可以按目錄順序閱讀，配合計算工具和實驗，逐步核對自己的理解。 遇到書中的算例，不妨先自己估一下，再看推導和實驗結果。也可以換成你正在使用的模型和硬體，看看結論是否改變。 配套計算與實驗 配套計算工具 可以用來複算書中的數字，也可以換一組模型和輸入，估算資源需求。工具附有模型配置和 結果索引 ，靜態計算只需 Python 3.10+ 標準庫，無需 GPU 或模型權重。 git clone https://github.com/bojieli/ai-infra-book.git cd ai-infra-book # 檢視模型支援情況 python3 calculations/calc.py models # 估算 Qwen3-8B 在 8192-token prefill 下的逐運算元資源需求 python3 calculations/calc.py forward --model qwen3-8b --tokens 8192 --format md 倉庫使用 Git LFS 儲存論文和較大的輸入與測量記錄，合計約 20 GB。為避免克隆時全部下載， .lfsconfig 預設跳過所有 LFS 檔案，工作區中只留下指標；正文、配圖和靜態計算都不需要它們。復現某個實驗時，只下載對應目錄： git lfs install
git lfs pull --include= " experiments/ch05/05-01/** " --exclude= " " 配套實驗 按章節存放在 experiments/chXX/XX-YY/ 中，每個實驗都附有執行方法、輸入條件和結果說明。需要 GPU 的實驗會註明硬體與依賴要求；沒有相應裝置，也可以先閱讀已有記錄。復現或引用結果時，請留意所用的書稿版本、模型、硬體和輸入參數。 本地構建 閱讀網站 （Python 3.10+）： python3 -m venv .venv-site source .venv-site/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r website/requirements.txt
python scripts/build_site.py
python scripts/check_site.py
python scripts/build_site.py --serve 預覽地址為 http://127.0.0.1:8000 ，簡體中文位於根目錄，英文、繁體中文和俄語分別位於 en/ 、 zh-tw/ 和 ru/ 。生成檔案位於 build/ ，詳細說明見 網站構建與釋出 。 全書 PDF 與 EPUB （另需 Pandoc、XeLaTeX 和字型）： bash book/build_pdf.sh # 簡體中文 → book/AI-Infra-Book.pdf bash book-en/build_pdf.sh # English → book-en/AI-Infra-Book-EN.pdf bash book-zh-tw/build_pdf.sh # 繁體中文 → book-zh-tw/AI-Infra-Book-ZH-TW.pdf python3 book/build_epub.py --edition zh # EPUB 只需 Pandoc 與 Poppler；--edition 可選 zh、en、zh-tw、ru 譯本配圖存於 Git LFS，構建前先下載： git lfs pull --include="book-en/images/**,book-zh-tw/images/**" --exclude="" 。依賴、字型及單章編譯方法見 PDF 編譯說明 。GitHub Actions 會檢查 Pull Request 的網站與各語言的 PDF、EPUB 構建；推送到 main 後自動釋出 Release（四種語言各含 PDF 與 EPUB）並部署四種語言的線上閱讀網站。 倉庫結構 目錄 內容 manuscripts/ 前言、十二章正文、配圖與繪圖指令碼 experiments/ github.title: nolly-studio/cult-ui

sudo chown -R 1000:1000 config db downloads logs cookies temp 啟用了 rootless Docker 或 userns-remap 時，請使用容器 UID 1000 實際對映到宿主機的
UID/GID；對映方式參見 Docker 官方文件 。 方案 B：本地執行 前置要求： Python 3.11+ FFmpeg yt-dlp py -3.11 - m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install - r requirements.txt
python app.py 訪問 http://127.0.0.1:5000 。 方案 C：Windows 便攜包 build-tools/ 提供 Windows 執行檔構建工具 官方 Windows Release 包通常已內建 FFmpeg / FFprobe 如果手工打包，保持 ffmpeg/ 目錄完整即可 方案 D：Telegram 轉發機器人（可選） Y2A-Auto-tgbot 是一個獨立的 Telegram 機器人：在 Telegram 裡直接傳送 YouTube 影片 / 播放列表連結，機器人會呼叫本服務的 /tasks/add_via_extension 介面提交上傳任務。它需要單獨部署，不會隨本專案一起啟動。 ⚠️ 公共例項不保證可用。 @Y2AAuto_bot 執行在個人 VPS 上，該伺服器已被牆，可能隨時無法訪問。需要長期、穩定使用時請自行部署。 自部署要點（Bot Token 建立、Token 作用範圍等完整說明見 Y2A-Auto-tgbot README ）： 在 Telegram 找 @BotFather ，傳送 /newbot 建立機器人，拿到 TG_BOT_TOKEN （形如 123456789:AAE... ） 克隆並啟動機器人： git clone https://github.com/fqscfqj/Y2A-Auto-tgbot.git cd Y2A-Auto-tgbot # 編輯 docker-compose.yml 填寫 TG_BOT_TOKEN（可選 ADMIN_TELEGRAM_IDS），然後： docker compose up -d 開啟本專案的 設定 → 運維與安全 → Telegram Bot API Token ，點選「生成 Token」並立即複製 y2a_tgbot_v1_... （明文只顯示一次） 在 Telegram 向新建的機器人傳送 /settings ，填寫 API 地址 （機器人所在網路能訪問到的本專案地址，例如同機 http://127.0.0.1:5000 ，跨機器 http://192.168.1.100:5000 ）和 API Token ，再點「🔬 測試」確認連線成功 測試通過後，直接給機器人傳送 YouTube 連結即可提交任務 該 Token 只允許呼叫 /tasks/add_via_extension ，無法訪問設定、日誌等其它介面，並且可以隨時在設定頁重置或撤銷。 配置說明 首次執行會自動生成 config/config.json 。推薦先配置以下幾類參數： 基礎與安全 AUTO_MODE_ENABLED ：無人值守自動投稿總開關，預設 false password_protection_enabled ：Web 密碼保護，預設 false LOGIN_MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS ：連續錯誤次數上限，預設 5 LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES ：鎖定時長，預設 15 LOGIN_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES ：登入空閒超時時長，預設 30 分鐘，最小 1 ，訪問受保護頁面會自動續期 UPLOAD_TARGET_DEFAULT ：預設投稿平臺，支援 acfun 、 bilibili 、 both UPLOAD_APPEND_REPOST_NOTICE ：是否自動追加轉載宣告，預設 true 賬號與網路 YOUTUBE_COOKIES_PATH ：YouTube Cookie 路徑 ACFUN_COOKIES_PATH ：AcFun Cookie 路徑 BILIBILI_COOKIES_PATH ：bilibili Cookie 路徑 BILIBILI_SUBMIT_API ：bilibili 投稿介面， auto （預設，優先必剪 PC 介面，失敗回退 Web）/ bcut_pc / web （手改成 bcut 等別名也會被歸一化後再儲存） YOUTUBE_PROXY_ENABLED / YOUTUBE_PROXY_URL ：YouTube 下載代理 YOUTUBE_API_PROXY_ENABLED / YOUTUBE_API_PROXY_URL ：YouTube 監控 API 獨立代理，不繼承下載代理 YOUTUBE_DOWNLOAD_THREADS ：下載執行緒數 YOUTUBE_THROTTLED_RATE ：下載速度限制 YOUTUBE_API_KEY ：YouTube Data API v3 金鑰，監控功能需要 FFMPEG_LOCATION ：自定義 FFmpeg 路徑 FFMPEG_AUTO_DOWNLOAD ：Windows 缺失時自動下載 FFmpeg，預設 true FFmpeg 版本要求：≥ 5.1。 字幕燒錄使用 -fps_mode cfr 控制幀率模式，
該選項在 FFmpeg 5.1 才引入（5.0 及更早只認已棄用的 -vsync ）。倉庫自帶的
與自動下載的 FFmpeg（BtbN latest）都遠高於該版本；但若通過 FFMPEG_LOCATION 指向 5.0 或更早的舊版本，軟體編碼路徑會因 Unrecognized option 'fps_mode' 直接失敗（非硬體編碼器沒有降級重試，任務會直接報錯）。 VIDEO_CPU_CODEC=x265 還額外要求該 FFmpeg 構建帶 libx265 （需 --enable-gpl --enable-libx265 ，BtbN 與倉庫自帶版本均滿足）。缺失時會自動降級為 libx264 並繼續燒錄，不會因缺庫而丟掉整條字幕。 AI 與投稿 OPENAI_API_KEY / OPENAI_BASE_URL / OPENAI_MODEL_NAME ：全域性 AI 配置 OPENAI_THINKING_ENABLED ：是否允許模型使用思考模式；關閉時優先發送廠商文件中的原生開關（DeepSeek Chat 用 thinking 、Responses 用 reasoning.effort=none ；Qwen Chat/Responses 用 enable_thinking ；MiMo Chat 用 thinking 、Responses 用 reasoning.effort=none ）。原生開關被端點以 400/422 拒絕時，會在同一請求內再嘗試標準 reasoning_effort=none / reasoning.effort=none ，全部形態都失敗才移除控制並記錄 warning；此時模型可能恢復預設思考行為。第三方閘道器上的 DeepSeek/Ling/混元沒有可靠原生開關，先嚐試標準參數，再嘗試通用 thinking 物件。通過反向代理訪問官方端點時無法從域名識別廠商，會按第三方順序逐個嘗試，但不會因此跳過關閉思考的嘗試。OpenAI o 系列 / GPT-5 等推理模型各代支援的 reasoning_effort 取值不同，本開關不會自動改寫，需在模型閘道器側控制 SUBTITLE_OPENAI_* ：字幕翻譯專用覆蓋配置，留空則回退全域性 SUBTITLE_QC_* ：字幕質檢專用覆蓋配置，留空則回退字幕翻譯 / 全域性配置 TRANSLATE_TITLE / TRANSLATE_DESCRIPTION / GENERATE_TAGS ：自動生成標題、簡介、標籤 RECOMMEND_PARTITION ：自動推薦分割槽 FIXED_PARTITION_ID / FIXED_PARTITION_ID_BILIBILI ：固定分割槽 YOUTUBE_UPLOADER_AS_FIRST_TAG ：將上傳者作為首標籤 PRESET_TAGS_ENABLED / PRESET_TAGS ：預設標籤，每行一個（也接受逗號、頓號、分號分隔）。啟用後預設標籤排在任務標籤之前， GENERATE_TAGS 開啟時 AI 只補齊剩餘名額；一份預設同時服務 AcFun（前 6 個、每個約 10 字）與 bilibili（最多 12 個、每個 20 字） AI 文本功能同時相容 OpenAI Chat Completions 與 Responses API。 OPENAI_BASE_URL 可填寫 API 根地址（例如 https://api.openai.com/v1 ，預設使用 Chat Completions）或完整的 /chat/completions 、 /responses 地址；填寫完整端點時會自動選擇協議並規範化。Responses 請求會自動轉換訊息、JSON 輸出格式、思考開關和 token 上限參數，返回值也會歸一化供翻譯、質檢、智慧分段等現有功能使用。當相容服務不支援 response_format 、token 上限參數、自定義 temperature 或特定指令角色時，系統會根據端點實際錯誤逐級協商；若閘道器只返回籠統的請求 schema github.title: assistant-ui/assistant-ui
github.abstract: Product · Documentation · Examples · Discord · Contact Sales The UX of ChatGPT in your React app 💬🚀 assistant-ui is an open-source TypeScript/React library to build production-grade AI chat experiences fast. Installation The fastest path is the CLI, which scaffolds a Next.js app or adds the styled components to an existing project: npx assistant-ui@latest create # new project npx assistant-ui@latest init # add to existing project Or install the packages directly: npm install @assistant-ui/react @assistant-ui/ai-sdk ai Usage "use client" ; import { AssistantRuntimeProvider } from "@assistant-ui/react" ; import { useChatRuntime } from "@assistant-ui/ai-sdk" ; import { Thread } from "@/components/assistant-ui/elements/thread.aui" ; export function Chat ( ) { const runtime = useChatRuntime ( ) ; return ( < AssistantRuntimeProvider runtime = { runtime } > < Thread /> </ AssistantRuntimeProvider > ) ; } useChatRuntime connects to the Vercel AI SDK out of the box. Swap it for useLangGraphRuntime , useDataStreamRuntime , or any custom runtime to integrate with your own backend. What you get Composable primitives : build any chat UX from Thread , Message , Composer , ThreadList , ActionBar , and friends. Style every pixel yourself, or start from a polished shadcn/ui theme that the CLI copies into your project. Production UX out of the box : streaming, auto-scroll, retries, attachments, markdown, code highlighting, voice dictation, keyboard shortcuts, and accessibility. Generative UI : render tool calls and JSON as React components, collect inline human approvals, and expose safe frontend actions to the model. Strong TypeScript : typed runtime APIs, tool schemas, message parts, and adapters end to end. Backends Integration Package Vercel AI SDK @assistant-ui/ai-sdk LangGraph / LangChain @assistant-ui/react-langgraph , @assistant-ui/react-langchain AG-UI / A2A protocols @assistant-ui/react-ag-ui , @assistant-ui/react-a2a Google ADK / OpenCode @assistant-ui/react-google-adk , @assistant-ui/react-opencode Custom data-stream backend @assistant-ui/react-data-stream Managed thread history, telemetry, and file storage assistant-cloud Broad model support out of the box (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Mistral, Perplexity, AWS Bedrock, Azure, Fireworks, Ollama) plus community providers via the AI SDK, and easy extension to any custom HTTP backend. Customization Instead of a single monolithic chat component, you compose primitives and bring your own styles. The CLI ships a great starter in your choice of Base UI (the default) or Radix UI flavor; you control everything else. Used in production by …and many more. Demos Community & Support Examples Documentation Discord Book a sales call License MIT, with optional Assistant Cloud for managed thread persistence and analytics. Backed by Y Combinator.

github.abstract: FastMCP 🚀 Move fast and make things. Made with 💙 by Prefect The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects LLMs to tools and data. FastMCP is a full MCP application framework for servers, clients, and interactive apps. A server starts with ordinary Python: from fastmcp import FastMCP mcp = FastMCP ( "Demo 🚀" ) @ mcp . tool def add ( a : int , b : int ) -> int : """Add two numbers""" return a + b if __name__ == "__main__" : mcp . run () Why FastMCP Building an effective MCP application is harder than it looks. FastMCP handles all of it. Declare a tool with a Python function, and the schema, validation, and documentation are generated automatically. Connect to a server with a URL, and transport negotiation, authentication, and protocol lifecycle are managed for you. You focus on your logic, and the MCP part just works: with FastMCP, best practices are built in. That's why FastMCP is the standard framework for working with MCP. FastMCP 1.0 was incorporated into the official MCP Python SDK in 2024. Today, the actively maintained standalone project is downloaded a million times a day, and some version of FastMCP powers 70% of MCP servers across all languages. FastMCP has three pillars: Servers Expose tools, resources, and prompts to LLMs. Apps Give your tools interactive UIs rendered directly in the conversation. Clients Connect to any MCP server — local or remote, programmatic or CLI. Servers wrap your Python functions into MCP-compliant tools, resources, and prompts. Clients connect to any server with full protocol support. And Apps give your tools interactive UIs rendered directly in the conversation. Building in TypeScript? FastMCP for TypeScript is the official counterpart, built and maintained by the same team. Same pillars, same ideas, npm install @prefecthq/fastmcp-ts . Ready to build? Start with the installation guide or jump straight to the quickstart . Scale MCP with FastMCP Gateway FastMCP handles the MCP application layer. FastMCP Gateway is the enterprise MCP gateway for scaling servers and tools across teams, with centralized governance over how they are deployed, discovered, secured, and used. FastMCP and FastMCP Gateway are built by the same team at Prefect . Deploy FastMCP servers from GitHub with branch previews and instant rollback. Create a private registry of every MCP your company uses. Secure access with SSO and tool-level RBAC. Get audit logs, observability, and governance across your MCP stack. Remix approved tools into purpose-built endpoints for teams and agents. Start with FastMCP. Scale with FastMCP Gateway → Installation We recommend adding FastMCP to your project with uv : uv add fastmcp For full installation instructions, including verification and upgrading, see the Installation Guide . Upgrading? We have guides for: Upgrading from FastMCP 3 Upgrading from FastMCP 2 Upgrading from MCP SDK v1 or v2 Upgrading from the low-level SDK v1 or v2 📚 Documentation FastMCP's complete documentation is available at gofastmcp.com , including detailed guides, API references, and advanced patterns. Documentation is also available in llms.txt format , which is a simple markdown standard that LLMs can consume easily: llms.txt is essentially a sitemap, listing all the pages in the documentation. llms-full.txt contains the entire documentation. Note this may exceed the context window of your LLM. Give your coding agent llms.txt as its starting point. See Coding Agents for version-matched documentation and the optional server authoring skill. Community: Join our Discord server to connect with other FastMCP developers and share what you're building. Contributing Start with CONTRIBUTING.md for accepted contributions and the issue-assignment workflow, then follow the Contributing Guide for setup and validation. Agents should read AGENTS.md .

An animation engine for explanatory math videos Manim is an animation engine for explanatory math videos. It's used to create precise animations programmatically, as demonstrated in the videos of 3Blue1Brown . Note The community edition of Manim (ManimCE) is a version maintained and developed by the community. It was forked from 3b1b/manim, a tool originally created and open-sourced by Grant Sanderson, also creator of the 3Blue1Brown educational math videos. While Grant Sanderson continues to maintain his own repository, we recommend this version for its continued development, improved features, enhanced documentation, and more active community-driven maintenance. If you would like to study how Grant makes his videos, head over to his repository ( 3b1b/manim ). Table of Contents: Installation Usage Documentation Docker Help with Manim Contributing License Installation Caution These instructions are for the community version only . Trying to use these instructions to install 3b1b/manim or instructions there to install this version will cause problems. Read this and decide which version you wish to install, then only follow the instructions for your desired version. Manim requires a few dependencies that must be installed prior to using it. If you
want to try it out first before installing it locally, you can do so in our online Jupyter environment . For local installation, please visit the Documentation and follow the appropriate instructions for your operating system. Usage Manim is an extremely versatile package. The following is an example Scene you can construct: from manim import * class SquareToCircle ( Scene ): def construct ( self ): circle = Circle () square = Square () square . flip ( RIGHT ) square . rotate ( - 3 * TAU / 8 ) circle . set_fill ( PINK , opacity = 0.5 ) self . play ( Create ( square )) self . play ( Transform ( square , circle )) self . play ( FadeOut ( square )) In order to view the output of this scene, save the code in a file called example.py . Then, run the following in a terminal window: manim -p -ql example.py SquareToCircle You should see your native video player program pop up and play a simple scene in which a square is transformed into a circle. You may find some more simple examples within this GitHub repository . You can also visit the official gallery for more advanced examples. Manim also ships with a %%manim IPython magic which allows to use it conveniently in JupyterLab (as well as classic Jupyter) notebooks. See the corresponding documentation for some guidance and try it out online . Command line arguments The general usage of Manim is as follows: The -p flag in the command above is for previewing, meaning the video file will automatically open when it is done rendering. The -ql flag is for a faster rendering at a lower quality. Some other useful flags include: -s to skip to the end and just show the final frame. -n <number> to skip ahead to the n 'th animation of a scene. -f show the file in the file browser. For a thorough list of command line arguments, visit the documentation . Documentation Documentation is in progress at ReadTheDocs . Docker The community also maintains a docker image ( manimcommunity/manim ), which can be found on DockerHub .
Instructions on how to install and use it can be found in our documentation . Help with Manim If you need help installing or using Manim, feel free to reach out to our Discord
Server or Reddit Community . If you would like to submit a bug report or feature request, please open an issue. Contributing Contributions to Manim are always welcome. In particular, there is a dire need for tests and documentation. For contribution guidelines, please see the documentation . However, please note that Manim is currently undergoing a major refactor. In general,
contributions implementing new features will not be accepted in this period.
The contribution guide may become outdated quickly; we highly recommend joining our Discord server to discuss any potential
contributions and keep up to date with the latest developments. Most developers on the project use uv for management. You'll want to have uv installed and available in your environment.
Learn more about uv at its documentation and find out how to install manim with uv at the manim dev-installation guide in the manim documentation. How to Cite Manim We acknowledge the importance of good software to support research, and we note
that research becomes more valuable when it is communicated effectively. To
demonstrate the value of Manim, we ask that you cite Manim in your work.
Currently, the best way to cite Manim is to go to our repository page (if you aren't already) and
click the "cite this repository" button on the right sidebar. This will generate
a citation in your preferred format, and will also integrate well with citation managers. Code of Conduct Our full code of conduct, and how we enforce it, can be read on our website . others.title: TRANSLATING POWER: AI, MEDIATION AND THE IMAGINARY OF MANIPULATION IN ACADEMIC CONTEXTS
others.abstract: The growing use of generative artificial intelligence in academic writing and translation is changing not only the speed of textual production but also the ways in which linguistic authority is constructed and perceived. In multilingual academic contexts, AI systems translate, reformulate, and refine texts according to dominant conventions of academic English. Such assistance may widen access to international communication, yet its fluency can also make the interpretative choices embedded in the resulting text less visible. This article examines AI-mediated Romanian-English academic translation as a site where linguistic assistance, symbolic power, and the imaginary of manipulation intersect. The study approaches translation as mediation rather than neutral transfer. It asks how AI may reshape lexical authority, epistemic stance, and stylistic identity, how these changes influence the perceived legitimacy of academic discourse, and when unobtrusive mediation may acquire a potentially manipulative effect. The theoretical discussion connects translation studies with scholarship on symbolic power, academic stance, and sociotechnical imaginaries. Methodologically, the article adopts a conceptual qualitative approach supported by three illustrative Romanian-English micro-analyses. These examples are not treated as a representative corpus and do not support statistical generalisation. Instead, they reveal how apparently minor lexical, epistemic, and stylistic reformulations can influence authority, certainty, and authorial visibility. The article argues that manipulation should not be equated automatically with factual distortion or deliberate ideological intent. It may also arise through naturalisation, when a fluent and plausible formulation is accepted as transparent or inevitable. The article concludes that responsible AI-assisted academic translation requires comparison with the source, attention to shifts in certainty, agency and rhetorical positioning, and clear human responsibility for the final text. For translators, writers and educators, critical AI literacy entails treating generated language as a proposal to be evaluated rather than as an impersonal solution.

others.title: VLM-DC: Vision--Language Model for Automotive Data Collection
others.abstract: The development of advanced driver-assistance systems (ADASs) and autonomous driving technologies depends on high-quality, representative driving data. Traditional collection methods either demand extensive manual filtering or rely on rigid thresholds that miss critical edge cases. To overcome these limitations and meet diverse operational and system requirements, this work introduces a two-module, vision–language model (VLM)-based framework for intelligent and targeted data collection. The first module employs a cloud–edge multiagent architecture, where a cloud-based large language model (LLM) coordinates sensor selection and an edge-deployed VLM evaluates scene relevance. This approach achieves 91.35% overall precision, reduces storage by 28.30%, and shows promising performance on geographically distinct out-of-distribution (OOD) datasets. The second module implements a distributed VLM architecture with knowledge distillation (KD), deploying a lightweight vision encoder on vehicles and a language decoder in the cloud. A selective token transfer mechanism reduces model size by 71% and bandwidth use by 50% while maintaining 91.86% overall accuracy. Both modules outperform larger baselines while remaining computationally and communication efficient. Overall, this framework shifts automotive data collection from exhaustive recording to selective capture of valuable driving moments, accelerating ADAS development and validation.

others.title: A new hash function based on irreversible finite automata
others.abstract: A mathematical hash function maps inputs of arbitrary length to unique outputs (digests) of a fixed length. It is highly useful and used in almost all information security applications; it can also serve as index data in hash tables, detect duplicate data for fingerprinting or uniquely identifying files, and serve as well for checksums to identify data corruption. In this work, a novel 256-bit cryptographic hash function based on the irreversible Mealy finite automata model (IFA) is introduced. In this architecture, the irreversible transition matrix of the Mealy automaton (IFA) is constructed using a non-injective state-transition mechanism to introduce local irreversibility and ambiguous backward reconstruction. The automaton output table is precomputed using a Chebyshev-based nonlinear generator to improve output randomness and nonlinear complexity. For further diffusion, confusion, collision resistance, and one-wayness improvements, we integrate the irreversible automaton within a sponge-based construction with a 512-bit internal state (256-bit rate + 256-bit capacity), yielding a designed collision resistance of bits and preimage resistance of under the sponge capacity bound. Evaluation against SHA-256 shows an avalanche mean of 50.02% (σ = 3.14%), all 13 NIST SP 800-22 statistical tests passed, and zero collisions among 50,000 tests. Throughput is about 13 MB/s versus 183 MB/s for SHA-256, reflecting the sequential dependency of the Mealy transformation.

others.title: Cybercrime law and digital forensics: adapting legal frameworks for future technologies
others.abstract: Linked authenticity, integrity, reliability, attribution, jurisdiction, and privacy challenges are created by digital evidence from cloud platforms, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, artificial intelligence (AI), large language models (LLMs), biometrics, drones, blockchain, and virtual environments. This review synthesizes scholarly and authoritative sources on cybercrime law, digital forensics, and emerging technologies through a structured narrative review. The review reveals a technical–legal divide: it emphasizes investigative efficiency, while acquisition, hashing, metadata, chain of custody, tool validation, and automated-analysis reliability require clarification for evidentiary scrutiny. Technology, evidence source, forensic challenge, legal risk, admissibility requirement, and governance response are linked through the Technology–Forensic–Legal Admissibility (TFLA) Framework. Primary artifacts are distinguished from analytical outputs; technical weaknesses are translated into legal consequences and safeguards. Standards and evidentiary rules are complemented; TFLA is conceptual, not empirically validated. Technology-neutral, technically informed, rights-compliant governance is supported through transparent documentation, corroboration, human oversight, and institutional competence. Digital-forensic system design is linked to trustworthy technology governance.

others.title: An Occlusion-Aware Decision-Making Framework With Cooperative Active Perception for Connected Automated Vehicles in Unsignalized Intersections
others.abstract: Occlusions at unsignalized intersections can hide safety-critical traffic participants and force autonomous vehicles (AVs) into overly conservative or unsafe decisions. Although cooperative perception among connected automated vehicles (CAVs) can partially alleviate this issue, its effectiveness remains limited because CAVs typically conduct passive sensing, which often leaves many risky occluded areas unresolved. This article proposes an occlusion-aware decision-making framework for CAVs considering cooperative active perception (CAP). It first conducts occlusion modeling using a directed-graph road representation and phantom vehicle model, which identifies risky occluded areas through conflict-point reasoning, spatiotemporal reachability analysis, and passive cooperative perception among CAVs. Remaining unobservable risky occlusions trigger active perception requests to nearby CAVs. Assisted CAVs then employ a finite-state-machine policy to select safe viewpoint-enhancing maneuvers based on surrounding traffic, occlusion type, and request urgency. In addition, the ego CAV plans conservatively using worst case reachable sets for phantom occluded vehicles before the remaining risky occluded areas are revealed, and upon receiving occlusion information, switches to selecting a safe speed range that enables efficient traversal. Simulation results and real-time co-simulation on dSPACE, a commercial high-fidelity vehicle-system validation platform, demonstrate that the proposed strategy can potentially improve computational efficiency and provide safe and efficient driving in unsignalized intersections.

others.title: GA-LLMSS: Text-Spatio–Temporal Graph-Guided and Cross-Modal Alignment-Enhanced Large Language Model Empowered Soft Sensor
others.abstract: Data-driven soft sensing has gained widespread application in modern industrial processes for real-time, low-cost estimation of key quality variables, but existing models are generally constrained by single-modal numerical inputs and limited representational generalization. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in time-series tasks due to their sequence-pattern generalization, textual reasoning, and cross-modal knowledge transfer abilities, yet their application in soft sensing remains limited. To bridge this gap, this article proposes a text-spatio–temporal graph-guided and cross-modal alignment-enhanced LLM-empowered two-stage soft sensor (GA-LLMSS). Specifically, a scale-adaptive spatio–temporal graph encoder (SASTGE) is developed, which reconstructs raw multivariate time series into dynamic spatio–temporal interaction graphs (STIGs) according to the nonstationary characteristics, injecting structured prior logic to compensate for LLMs’ inherent deficiency in intervariable spatial perception. Building on this, a prompt-enhanced graph construction (PEGC) module enriches input semantics by crafting industrial prior knowledge prompts (IPKPs) with higher-order statistics, while an anchor token then serves as a cross-modal hub to establish logic-guided edges between prompts and graph nodes that explicitly guide LLMs in capturing cross-modal logical relationships and maintaining semantic coherence. To bridge textual and time-series modalities, an improved representation learning, dropout autoregressive alignment stage (DAAS), is proposed to enforce learning of deep spatio–temporal couplings from incomplete observations. Finally, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) adapts the model to real-world industrial scenarios: air preheaters (APs) and gas turbines (GTs). Experiments show that GA-LLMSS achieves advanced accuracy, superior few-shot representation generalization, and ablation studies validate the independent contributions of each key module.

others.title: Brain Cognition-Inspired Adaptable LLM Agents for Continuous Knowledge Reuse Across Tasks in IoT
others.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are promising in Internet of Things (IoT) applications. However, existing agent systems suffer from an ephemeral limitation: agents are instantiated for individual tasks and terminated upon completion, losing valuable execution experiences across different tasks where past knowledge reuse is impossible. Inspired by dual-process theory in cognitive science, we propose a brain cognition-inspired dual-system agent framework for continuous knowledge reuse across heterogeneous task streams, termed the cognition-inspired dual-system agent framework for continuous knowledge reuse (CIA-CKR). The CIA-CKR framework separates fast (reactive execution) from slow (deliberative planning) cognition phases by maintaining a persistent knowledge base throughout the operational lifetime of agents. Two synergistic mechanisms are designed that mirror bidirectional knowledge flow in human cognition: a personalized agent generation mechanism that retrieves task-relevant knowledge and configures context-specific agent capabilities through top-down adaptation, and a knowledge accumulation mechanism that extracts experiential insights from execution traces through bottom-up feedback. Extensive experiments on HomeBench (smart home control) and OmniEAR (embodied multiagent collaboration) datasets demonstrate that CIA-CKR consistently outperforms both vanilla LLMs and recent memory-augmented methods, achieving 10.82% and 4.23% average accuracy improvements on HomeBench and OmniEAR, respectively, over the best baselines.
